support_floor.reason: Zero-support floor: a UC payment-distribution band or a benefit-cap amount band whose compiled matrix row reaches no source household (household_source_id) with a positive prior weight cannot be fitted by any weights (the solver's initialiser refuses a nonzero target with no support), so it is dropped from the solve, not pooled. A row that some households carry stays bound however few they are; when fewer than 10 distinct source households carry it, its model figures are withheld from every written surface (the UK Data Service working floor, CD171 section 5.2.1). The floor's receipt reports each target's dropped published total, and the run refuses when the drops pass either ceiling or when a per-row exclusion names a row the floor drops.
support_floor.adjudication: microcosm#1095 U3, ruled 2026-10-16 with the fifth ports PR (floor 10) and revised 2026-10-21 with #1333: a cell that rests on fewer than 10 records is no reason to leave a row out, only a measured distortion of the calibration is. The floor drops only rows no household carries, the benefit-cap amount bands join its scope and their per-row entries retire, and the figures of rows under 10 source households are withheld, as the BRMA rows' are. The thirteen entries it retired (the eleven benefit-cap amount bands and the two HMRC £500k to £1m cells) and the A/B that retired them: experiments/1095-uk-thin-row-binding-receipts.md.

exclusions.name: obr.housing_benefit
exclusions.reason: Frame-side gap, not a weight question, decomposed on 2026-09-16 (spine-q design weights unless stated). FRS 2024-25 reports 1.56m Housing Benefit benefit units, 99.9 percent renters, near the DWP GB caseload (1.94m in January 2025 falling to 1.46m by December); the spine carries 1.21m GB reporters (GBP 7.15bn reported) because the SPI support channel re-imputes benefit receipt onto its synthetic households without tenure coherence: 363k of its 449k reporting units sit in owner-occupied households and can never be paid. The engine then pays Housing Benefit only to reporting units with a rented tenure, not drawn into Universal Credit, under the capital limit and carrying the household's rent (rent is the household head's benefit unit's alone; claims_all_entitled_benefits collapses to a scalar, so there is no take-up lever): 407k all-pension-age reporting units were drawn into Universal Credit by the 55 percent take-up draw although they cannot claim it, and the working-age remainder is pared by the means test. On the Q50f candidate the engine pays 235k units and GBP 2.13bn against the OBR GBP 12.10bn (-82 percent); the U8 lever receipt already showed the same lever from the other side (0.85 take-up moved this row from -0.0 to -52.4 percent). This PR gates the draw to units with an adult under State Pension age; the SPI-channel tenure defect is a #840/#145 item; the OBR line also carries supported and temporary accommodation the frame has no concept for. Re-measured on every evaluation with the three Housing Benefit caseload rows; renew or retire on the next spine that carries the SPI repair.
exclusions.adjudication: microcosm#882 (the 2026-09-16 status comment, issuecomment-5694598278, whose next-steps list this repair works, and the repairs plan María approved on 2026-09-16 with her population ruling on the U8 take-up entry; approver as author per the register convention). Expiry 2026-12-08 aligns the whole UC-repair tranche with the zero-band clock already on the register (microcosm#877), so the next spine re-adjudicates them together. Receipts: experiments/882-uc-repairs-receipts.md (R1 and R5, tools/diagnose_uk_legacy_benefits.py on spine-q, the Q50f candidate, FRS 2024-25 and the twins).

exclusions.reason: Frame-side gap, not a weight question, decomposed on 2026-09-16. DWP's 71,000 claimants at August 2025 is New Style (contributory) JSA after the August 2025 methodology change that removed inactive claims. FRS 2024-25 reports 63k JSA benefit units at design weights (37k contributory, 23k income-based; 27 records), so the source reproduces the DWP count. The spine carries 178k contributory and 92k income-based reporters (GB, design weights) because the SPI support channel re-imputes benefit receipt onto its synthetic households: 161k of the 181k contributory reporters sit there. The stage-6 legacy_jobseeker_proxy (967k) is consumed by nothing. On the Q50f candidate the row measures 34k against 71,000 (-52 percent) after the solve pares the reporters to fit the OBR JSA spend line. The repair is the SPI channel's benefit-receipt fill (#840/#145), not a JSA rule; the income-based reporters are a legacy-scheme residual DWP no longer counts. Renew or retire on the next spine that carries the SPI repair.

exclusions.name: dwp.uc.households_housing_element
exclusions.reason: Structural bias, not a weight question: DWP's any-tenure housing-entitlement count is social plus private plus 'Other or unknown' tenure, and the model has no other/unknown tenure (uc_housing_costs_element pays only council, housing-association and private renters), so the model's any-tenure count is identically the social plus private rows, which are bound and fit; the row overstates the reachable total by the other/unknown cell, 112,518 of 4,037,650 in calendar 2025 (2.8 percent; the published any-tenure mean, which the three tenure cells reproduce to the unit). Fitting all three housing rows would ask the solver to over-fill the tenure rows by that amount. Measured on every evaluation as the housing-element caseload diagnostic (Q50f -0.8 percent, D2 +0.6 percent at the baseline; v20 -2.8 percent unbound, the structural gap itself, docs/evidence/uk-a16-v20/).
exclusions.adjudication: microcosm#882 (element sizing at the 10 September 2026 baseline, docs/uk-uc-baseline-2026-09-10.md; María's sign-off in review of microcosm#921 on 2026-09-15, setting the one-month window); renewed one month on 2026-10-14 by juaristi22 in session (microcosm#1124 local release): the model still has no other/unknown tenure, so the any-tenure count stays structurally above the bound tenure rows

exclusions.name: obr.vat
exclusions.reason: Level set by an engine factor, not the weights: policyengine-uk's vat divides household VAT by gov.simulation.microdata_vat_coverage (0.38, a constant since January 2023 with no recorded derivation; policyengine-uk#1996), which folds the household share of VAT receipts (about 70 percent per OBR and the HMRC VAT gap estimates) together with the survey's capture of household spending. The frame's raw household VAT is about 46 percent of the OBR receipts, so the row reads +24.7 percent at design weights and +24.1 percent calibrated on microcosm#1121's head calibration (policyengine-uk 2.122.2), against the 25 percent bound. On the 2026-09-30 national problem (1,090 rows, before this stage set any level) the calibration with the four consumption-tax rows bound left total consumption GBP 55bn (5 percent) below a re-solve with the four consumption-tax rows masked together (GBP 982bn against GBP 1,037bn). In that re-solve the other 1,086 rows fitted no worse (98.5 against 98.4 percent within 10 percent, none past 25 percent against one). Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; rebind when a locked policyengine-uk splits the factor into the published household share and a declared survey capture and the row fits.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-08 on the VAT, road fuel and domestic energy plan (microcosm#1113, microcosm#1123 item 3), decision D3: hold the row out until the engine factor is split. The reason's figures were restated on 2026-10-11 after her review of PolicyEngine/microcosm#1167, which found bases mixed. Receipts: experiments/1113-consumption-tax-levels-receipts.md (the masked re-solve of the 2026-09-30 problem and microcosm#1121's head calibration). Tracking moved from policyengine-uk#1996 to microcosm#1278 on 2026-10-20: policyengine-uk#2187, released in 2.135.7, closed #1996, and main locks 2.134.4, so the rebind waits on a lock bump past 2.135.7, after the Budget.

exclusions.name: ons.household_electricity_expenditure
exclusions.reason: Published-source residual, not a weight question: the lcfs_consumption stage sets electricity spend from the DESNZ Energy Trends domestic volume over the four quarters of calendar 2024 at QEP calendar-2024 average prices paid (the level the energy_rake gate checks), and ONS Consumer Trends 04.5.1 sits below it on every aligned basis. For calendar 2024 it is GBP 26.10bn against the stage's GBP 29.52bn on microcosm#1121's head spine (0.88). For calendar 2025 it is GBP 26.52bn against GBP 29.60bn for Energy Trends volume times QEP unit and fixed costs (0.90), and 1.11 times unit cost alone; meters against households explains about 2 percent. On the 2026-09-30 national problem the calibration took electricity from GBP 29.11bn at design weights to GBP 26.54bn (8.8 percent; 93.0 to 82.9 TWh, 10.9 percent). In a re-solve with the four consumption-tax rows masked together it stayed at GBP 28.70bn, and the other 1,086 rows fitted no worse. Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; retire if the reconciliation microcosm#1278 tracks finds a concept difference to bridge.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-08 on the VAT, road fuel and domestic energy plan (microcosm#1113, microcosm#1123 item 3), decision D1: DESNZ volume at QEP prices stays the level and the ONS rows become diagnostics. The reason was restated on the calendar-2024 basis on 2026-10-10 with her approval, after her ruling of 2026-10-09 put every LCFS spend column at calendar-2024 prices. Its figures were restated on 2026-10-11 after her review of PolicyEngine/microcosm#1167, which found bases mixed. Receipts: experiments/1113-consumption-tax-levels-receipts.md.

exclusions.reason: Published-source residual, not a weight question: the lcfs_consumption stage sets gas spend from the DESNZ Energy Trends domestic volume over the four quarters of calendar 2024 at QEP calendar-2024 average prices paid over the published gas-connected share, and ONS Consumer Trends 04.5.2 sits below it on every aligned basis. For calendar 2024 it is GBP 14.64bn against the stage's GBP 19.23bn on microcosm#1121's head spine (0.76). Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; retire if the reconciliation microcosm#1278 tracks finds a concept difference to bridge.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-08 on the VAT, road fuel and domestic energy plan (microcosm#1113, microcosm#1123 item 3), decision D1: DESNZ volume at QEP prices stays the level and the ONS rows become diagnostics. exclusions.name: obr.fuel_duties_cars
exclusions.reason: Scope and conversion residual once the stage sets household road fuel: OBR's cars receipts (GBP 14.4bn for FY2024-25, the April 2024 vehicle-type split) include car fuel paid by businesses, and ONS Consumer Trends 07.2.2 for CY2025 at DESNZ 2025 pump prices converts to about GBP 13.5bn of duty, 7 percent below the OBR cars line. With petrol plus diesel levelled to ONS 07.2.2 by the lcfs_consumption stage, the engine's 2025 fuel_duty reads -9.9 percent against the row on its RAC price divisors (-8.1 percent on DESNZ's; policyengine-uk#2169 A), so binding it would pull weight toward fuel buyers to cover business use the household frame does not hold. Before the level step it read -34.5 percent at design weights and -17.7 percent calibrated on microcosm#1121's head, where the weights raised petrol 21 and diesel 34 percent from design to final. On the 2026-09-30 national problem the calibration with the four consumption-tax rows bound left petrol 18 and diesel 36 percent above a re-solve with the four consumption-tax rows masked together, in which the other 1,086 rows fitted no worse. Household road fuel is bound as ons.household_road_fuel_expenditure. Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; rebind if Microcosm comes to model business use of cars, which microcosm#1278 tracks.
exclusions.adjudication: María's approval of 2026-10-08 of the VAT, road fuel and domestic energy plan (microcosm#1113, microcosm#1123 item 3), decision D2, with the binding confirmed on 2026-10-09: the stage sets the household road-fuel level and incidence, and the household-scope ONS 07.2.2 row is bound in place of the OBR cars receipts, which include business fuel. The reason's figures were restated on 2026-10-11 after her review of PolicyEngine/microcosm#1167, which found bases mixed. Receipts: experiments/1113-consumption-tax-levels-receipts.md.

exclusions.name: obr.ni_employer
exclusions.reason: Engine and period basis for roughly half of the gap; the rest is under investigation. policyengine-uk's ni_employer is the secondary Class 1 charge on each earner's pay above the secondary threshold, gross of the Employment Allowance, which employers offset against their secondary Class 1 liability through payroll, so OBR's receipts are net of it: HMRC's tax relief statistics (January 2026) put its cost at GBP 7.4bn for 2025-26 (a forecast), after the allowance rose to GBP 10,500 per employer and the GBP 100,000 eligibility restriction was removed from 6 April 2025. The row also binds the calendar-2025 window of the OBR fiscal years (three twelfths of FY2024-25, nine twelfths of FY2025-26), while the engine's 2025 period applies the FY2025-26 rules (the 15 percent rate and the GBP 5,000 secondary threshold) to the whole window, so its first quarter is overstated. On the K=15 local candidates measured for microcosm#1301 the row read about 20 percent above its target: the allowance accounts for about a quarter of that excess, the window for about a fifth and the under-21 zero rate, which the engine also omits, for under a tenth, so the stated parts explain roughly half of it. The rest sits in the pay level and may be a conflict between the bound pay targets and OBR's NICs base rather than a weighting defect. Bound, the row pulls pay down against those pay targets to close a gap at least half of which the weights did not open. Held out of the objective as a diagnostic and never fitted; rebind when a locked policyengine-uk nets the allowance out of ni_employer and the window takes each fiscal year's own rules.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-16 on the microcosm#1301 local release plan: unbind the row as a measured diagnostic, rather than bind the FY2025-26 value or sign it gate-only, because modelling the allowance alone would close only part of the gap. The exclusion applies on both lines, since this register has no line scoping: the national objective drops the row too, and a national run given a frozen scoring register derived before this entry fails closed (the re-derived register differs from the frozen one), so the national build's frozen register is derived from a head that carries this entry. policyengine-uk#2459, split from policyengine-uk#1918 (which keeps the under-21 and apprentice zero rates), asks the engine to net the allowance out of ni_employer. The expiry gives the three-month window of the 2026-10-08 engine-factor diagnostic (obr.vat).

exclusions.name: orr.rail_government_support
exclusions.reason: Basis, not a weight question: the row binds ORR table 7270's broad total of government support to the Great Britain railway, and the frame's household rail subsidy (rail_subsidy_spending, the engine's rail_usage times gov.dft.rail.fare_index) sits far below it at design weights. Bound, the solve closes the gap by moving weight onto rail-using households, which also moves untargeted columns that correlate with rail use. Whether the household subsidy is measured against table 7270's broad total or table 7271's narrower by-source series is an open ruling (microcosm#890 G, microcosm#736). Held out of the objective as a measured diagnostic and never fitted; rebind on that ruling, against the narrower series in the feed or a column scaled as uk-data scales it.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-20 on the pre-Budget PR (microcosm#1278): hold the row out only if a national arm with it held out, run beside the calibration-period fix's arm (microcosm#1324), passes the gates and keeps the share of rows within 10 percent; otherwise keep it bound and label the distributional tables. The 7270-versus-7271 basis ruling stays open (microcosm#890 G). The expiry, 2026-12-11, matches the uprating holds' renewal, after the Budget.
